title: Implement a binary search tree in Rust
description: Implement BST<T: Ord> with insert, contains, and in_order traversal.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement BST<T: Ord> in src/lib.rs:
- Node<T>: val T, left/right Option<Box<Node<T>>>
- BST<T>: root Option<Box<Node<T>>>
- `insert`: recursive: if val < node.val go left, if val > go right, if == do nothing (no duplicates)
- `contains`: recursive: if val == return true; if < go left; if > go right; None = false
- `in_order`: in-order DFS returning references in sorted order
All 3 tests must pass.
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test --quiet` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `cargo test --quiet` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
